intro: Lazur is a voice AI assistant for the Mac that helps with Photoshop. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud and circles the control you need. It does not click for you, and it is not a plugin, so you stay in charge of the file.
tldr: Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about what is on screen in Photoshop. Lazur answers out loud and can circle a control.
Use guide mode for step by step help. Lazur waits for each click, and you do the clicking.
Lazur does not click, edit files or run Photoshop for you. It is not a plugin or add-in.
Check macOS before you install. CGChannel reports that Photoshop 27.11 needs macOS 14.0 or later.

blocks.text: Most people who search for an AI assistant for Photoshop on Mac want one thing. They want an answer while they work, without leaving the file. Lazur is built for that. It lives in the notch at the top of your screen. You hold ⌥ ⌘, ask a question, and let go.

While you hold the keys, Lazur looks at the screen and listens. When you let go, it answers out loud. Photoshop does not need a plugin for this. Lazur works from outside the app, the same way it works in Mail, Figma or a browser.
What Lazur does in Photoshop on Mac
Lazur has a few modes. Each one matches a different kind of question. Pick the question first, and the mode usually follows.

items: Explain: ask what a panel, slider, warning or dialog does.
Point: ask where a control is. Lazur circles it on screen and adds a label.
Guide: ask how to finish a task. Lazur gives one step at a time and waits for each click.
Draft: ask for words. Lazur types the draft at your cursor.
Dictate: hold fn and speak. Clean, formatted text lands at the cursor in any app.

blocks.text: Lazur also handles everyday tasks, such as Apple Reminders, Calendar events, timers and opening apps. Those are useful when you want a reminder to export the file. They are not the focus of this page.
Ask what is on screen in Photoshop
Explain mode is the one you will use most. Photoshop shows a lot at once. Panels, sliders, badges and warnings compete for your attention. When one confuses you, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about it directly.

Good questions name the thing you can see. 'What does this warning mean?' works well. 'What's wrong?' gives Lazur very little to go on. Narrow questions get narrow answers, and that is usually what you want in the middle of an edit.

Lazur answers from what it sees and from general knowledge of Photoshop. It cannot see files you have not opened. If an answer depends on your exact build, open Photoshop > About Photoshop and check the version. Then ask again with that version in mind.

blocks.title: Read the version first
blocks.text: Adobe changes menus between releases. Before you follow a menu path from a tutorial, check the version. A path written for an older build may not match Photoshop 2026.
Point at a control you cannot find

Finding layers is one of the common problems in the Puget Systems guide. That guide is dated March 26, 2024, and it has no frequency data. Treat it as a checklist, not a census. The problem is still real, and many people hit it in their first week.

Ask 'Where is the Layers panel?' and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. You then move your own mouse there. Lazur does not move the cursor for you. That gap matters. You learn the layout as you go, and the file stays open the whole time.
A worked example with a layer mask

Say you want to hide part of a photo without erasing it. You want a layer mask. Ask 'Where is the add layer mask button?' Lazur circles the icon at the bottom of the Layers panel. Click it yourself, then ask your next question.
If the Layers panel is closed, ask where it lives. Lazur can give you the menu path, which is Window > Layers. Open the panel, then ask again if you still cannot see the button.
When a shortcut beats pointing

Point mode is good for controls you rarely use. For keys you press every day, memorize them. The shortcut table later on this page lists the most useful Mac commands. Ask Lazur about any shortcut you do not know.
Walk through a feature one click at a time

Guide mode is for tasks with several steps. You tell Lazur the goal. It gives you the first step, then it waits. You click, then ask for the next step. The pace is slower than a video, but you see each dialog before it changes.
A Curves adjustment makes a good test. A typical session looks like this.

items: Ask how to add a Curves adjustment without changing the photo underneath.
Lazur points you to Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Curves, then waits.
Open the menu yourself and select Curves.
Drag the curve. If the result looks wrong, ask what that point does before you change anything else.

blocks.text: Guide works best when you give a goal, not a menu path. Say 'I want the sky darker without touching the people.' Lazur can then suggest a route, such as a layer mask, and walk you through it one step at a time.
If a step does not match your screen, stop and say so. Ask 'What does this slider do?' before you guess. A wrong guess early can change the whole adjustment, and it is harder to trace later.

blocks.title: Do not ask for the whole job
blocks.text: Lazur waits for each click, so one huge request means many turns. Split the job into stages, such as selection, adjustment and export. Each stage is easier to check.
Draft text at the cursor and dictate in Photoshop

Text shows up in more places in Photoshop than you might expect. It appears in text layers on the canvas, in file names, in export dialogs and in description fields. Each place needs a text cursor before you speak.

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. Dictation is unlimited on both Lazur plans. It works best when you click into the field first, so the cursor sits where you want the words.

Draft mode is for words you need to write. Say 'Draft a short caption for a ceramic mug photo.' Lazur types the draft at your cursor. Read it, change it and only then move on. You still decide what goes out.

A few extras help with repeat work. Snippets store text you type often. A personal dictionary holds names, product codes and words a speech tool may spell wrong. Clipboard slots keep more than one item ready at a time.

blocks.title: Check where the words went
blocks.text: Dictation goes wherever the cursor sits. If you speak with nothing selected, check the screen before you keep typing. A moved cursor sends words to the wrong place.
Photoshop problems people search for and where Lazur helps

The most useful problem list I could open came from a third party. Puget Systems lists 13 common Photoshop problems in its troubleshooting guide. It starts with slow performance, which the guide links to high RAM use. Trouble finding layers comes next, followed by files that will not save.
Adobe's own most-visited help topics were not available to check. This list is a starting point, not proof of what most people struggle with. Use it to match a symptom to a fix.

rows: Usually high RAM use, per Puget Systems
Explain: ask what a memory or performance message means. Lazur does not change your settings.
Listed as a common problem, no cause given
Point: Lazur circles the Layers panel and gives the menu path.
Often Indexed Color mode, per Puget Systems
Explain the message, then guide the mode change through Image > Mode.
Explain the warning. Adobe's May 2026 beta notes also fixed a false Mac scratch disk warning.
Explain the steps in the guide. Lazur cannot repair a crash.
blocks.caption: Problems from Puget Systems' guide, with what Lazur can and cannot do.

blocks.text: Puget's guide does not rank these by how often they happen. The order is the one the author chose. Read it as a checklist, not a set of odds.
Scratch disk warnings on Mac

The May 2026 beta notes list fixes for Mac. One stops adjustment dialogs from blocking the Discover panel. Another fixes a false scratch disk warning on Mac. The notes list no macOS requirements, so they do not tell you which Mac to use.

If you see a scratch disk message, ask Lazur what it means. Then check the free space on the disk you use for scratch files. A false warning and a full disk can look alike at first, so read the message closely.
Fix a Photoshop file that will not save
A common case is an indexed file that refuses to save in the format you need. Puget lists Indexed Color mode as a frequent cause. Here is a safe path for the next time it happens.

items: Choose File > Save As and save a copy under a new name first.
Ask Lazur to explain the message on screen.
If Lazur confirms Indexed Color is the cause, choose Image > Mode > RGB Color.
Try the save again, then check the colors before you overwrite anything.

blocks.text: Changing the mode can shift colors and remove some features. That is why the copy comes first. Keep the original untouched until the new file looks right.
If the save still fails, ask Lazur to read the exact text of the dialog. Write that text down. A short, exact message is easier to trace than a summary from memory.

blocks.title: Never convert the only copy
blocks.text: Converting the original and saving over it removes the indexed version. You then have to undo work to get it back, and undo history does not always reach that far.
Shortcuts worth learning on Mac
Shortcuts cut the number of questions you need to ask. The table below lists useful Mac shortcuts from Noble Desktop's Photoshop CC list.

blocks.caption: Mac shortcuts from Noble Desktop's list. Confirm each one in your version.

blocks.text: That page is undated and third party. Check each shortcut against your own menus before you rely on it. The ⌘F entry is the one people trip on. In Photoshop it reruns the last filter, not a search, so expect a change to the image.
Ask Lazur for the shortcut you need. Say 'What's the shortcut for fit on screen?' Lazur answers out loud and explains what the shortcut does. It does not press the keys for you.
What Lazur does not do in Photoshop

Setting expectations saves time. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate Photoshop for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Photoshop or any other app. It works from outside the app, the same way it works elsewhere on your Mac.

items: It will not apply a filter or change a layer for you.
It will not open or save your file.
It will not change your Photoshop preferences.
It only sees the screen while you hold the shortcut, so it cannot follow your work between questions.

blocks.text: That split is useful. Lazur explains, points and waits. You do the work. You keep control of the file, the settings and every save.
Privacy and what leaves your Mac
Photoshop files often hold client work. Before you ask Lazur anything, know what it sees. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut.

When you ask a question, the audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked and did is kept on the Mac.

blocks.title: Check the screen first
blocks.text: While you hold ⌥ ⌘, Lazur can see whatever is on screen. Close or hide client files with private details before you ask a question about your work.
Requirements for Photoshop and Lazur on Mac

Photoshop 27.11 is the newest release I could open. Adobe calls the current line Photoshop 2026. CGChannel reported 27.11 on October 6, 2026. It says the release runs on Windows 10 and later, and on macOS 14.0 or later.
Check your macOS version before you install. Choose Apple menu > About This Mac. If your Mac runs an older macOS, use the newest Photoshop release that your Mac supports, and read its release notes.
Lazur runs on Mac with Apple silicon or Intel. Windows support is planned, not available. Lazur does not change what your Mac can run, so the macOS check still applies to Photoshop.
Generative features in Photoshop cost credits. Enhance Edge costs 20 credits per use in 27.11. That meter belongs to Photoshop. Lazur's plan limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing).
Adobe's Photoshop product page gives no version number and no user count. This page does not give one either.
Common mistakes with an AI assistant in Photoshop

items: Asking for a result instead of a method. Ask how, then do the step yourself.
Expecting Lazur to click. It points and waits, so keep your hand on the mouse.
Asking about a panel you have hidden. Open the panel first, then ask.
Dictating with no text field selected. Click into the field first.
Trusting a menu path from memory. Confirm it on your own Mac.
Changing the mode of the only copy of a file.

blocks.text: Most of these come from treating Lazur as an operator. It is a guide. The sooner you think of it that way, the less friction you feel during an edit.
Where to start this week

items: Download Lazur from the [download page](/download). Open it once to start the trial.
Open a file you already know, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what one panel does.
Ask for one shortcut each day until the common ones stick.
Dictate one short caption with fn, then read it before you use it.

faq.question: How does Lazur fit with Photoshop?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Photoshop or any other app. It runs on the Mac and works from outside Photoshop, the same way it works in other apps. You hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask a question, and Lazur answers out loud.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or edit my Photoshop file?
faq.answer: No. Lazur explains, points, guides you one click at a time and drafts or types text. You click, change settings and save the file yourself.

faq.question: Which Photoshop version does this page cover?
faq.answer: The newest release I could open is Photoshop 27.11, which Adobe brands as Photoshop 2026. CGChannel reported it on October 6, 2026. Check the release notes for any newer build.

faq.question: Which Macs can run Photoshop 27.11?
faq.answer: CGChannel says 27.11 needs macOS 14.0 or later. Check Apple menu > About This Mac before you install. Lazur runs on Macs with Apple silicon and Intel processors.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my whole screen all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer your question, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Why does Photoshop say it cannot save my file?
faq.answer: Puget Systems lists files that cannot be saved as a common problem, and it names Indexed Color mode as a frequent cause. Ask Lazur to explain the message. Save a copy first, then check Image > Mode before you change anything.

faq.question: Can I dictate into Photoshop with Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Click into the text field, then hold fn to dictate. Clean, formatted text appears at the cursor in any app. Dictation is unlimited on both Lazur plans.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows support is planned, but it is not available. Lazur is for the Mac.
